title: Optimize quantized inference kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion, KV-cache scheduling, and continuous batching
author: Evelyn Wang
ci_status: pass (initial perf job failed, rerun green)
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token overhead and improve throughput/latency for quantized inference (INT8/FP8) on common decoder workloads. We observed dequantize->GEMM->requantize paths adding significant overhead in the INT8/FP8 serving code path, especially when using smoothquant-style per-channel scaling. This PR fuses the dequantization and GEMM stages into a single kernel when possible, implements an FP8-aware path, improves KV-cache placement/scheduling to reduce remote cache misses, and tweaks the continuous batching policy to better prioritize interactive (low-latency) requests while preserving high throughput for batch jobs.

Changes in this PR:
- New fused kernel: runtime/kernel/quantized_fused_gemm.cu implements a fused dequant->gemm->(optional)requant pipeline supporting INT8 and FP8 inputs with smoothquant scale handling. Avoids temporary buffers for dequantized activations and reduces memory bandwidth.
- SmoothQuant support: runtime/kernel/smoothquant_utils.h/.cu add utilities to compute channel scales and apply them inside the fused kernel to preserve accuracy with INT8/FP8 quantization.
- Requantization fallbacks: If requantization to a model's storage format is required we do a final lightweight fused pass; otherwise we keep activations in the working format to avoid re-quantize/demote costs.
- KV-cache scheduling: runtime/scheduler/kvcache_placement.cc improves worker affinity for cached KV shards and uses a best-effort local-cache first policy to reduce cross-GPU transfer latency for streaming requests.
- Continuous batching: runtime/scheduler/continuous_batching.cc updates to an adaptive target batch size algorithm that reduces batching window for interactive routes and increases dynamic batching for background/pipeline workloads.
- Tests/benchmarks: tests/bench/quant_perf_bench.py and perf-canary/bench_scripts/quant_smoketest.sh add microbenchmarks and canary comparisons for INT8/FP8 fused path vs baseline.
- Documentation: docs/release_notes.md updated with performance numbers and rollout notes.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Feature gated behind runtime config flag "enable_quant_fused_gemm" (default: false). Config rollout planned: enable for Dedicated canaries first, roll to hosted after 2 weeks of telemetry.
- Provides safe FP16 fallback when a fused path fails or model uses unsupported operators.

Benchmarks (internal microbench, A100/RTX8000 mix, 2048-token-ish sequences):
- End-to-end token throughput: +28% for INT8 workloads, +18% for FP8 workloads vs previous quantized path.
- Median request latency (99th percentile): -12% for interactive streams when kvcache affinity enabled and continuous batching tuned.
- CPU/GPU memory traffic: ~24% reduction in host-device bandwidth for fused paths.
- Quantization accuracy (perplexity) change: <0.7% delta vs baseline (within acceptable regression threshold defined in ENG-3456).

Why this change matters:
- Removes a common per-token memory copy/dequantize overhead and takes advantage of fused compute to improve kernel utilization.
- SmoothQuant-specific handling keeps quantization quality high while enabling aggressive int8/fp8 performance.
- Better KV-cache locality reduces tail latency for streaming requests, which is critical for interactive features.
- Continuous batching improvements allow us to jointly optimize for interactive latency and bulk throughput without a hard service-level tradeoff.

release_notes:
- performance: fused INT8/FP8 dequant->GEMM kernel (runtime/kernel/quantized_fused_gemm.cu) improves token throughput by ~20-30% for quantized models.
- perf: KV-cache placement affinity reduces streaming tail latency by ~10-15% in canaries.
- batching: adaptive continuous batching adjusts window per-route to lower latency for interactive routes while preserving throughput for background jobs.
- rollout: gated behind runtime flag 'enable_quant_fused_gemm'; enablement plan: Dedicated canaries -> Hosted gradual rollout.
